text:
Alex P: Quick check-in on the metering incident follow-up. Need a clear step list for recomputing tokens, approval gates for invoice edits, and a plan to avoid recurrence. Short sync?
Mira K: I updated the postmortem with an owners table. @Sam G can you own the recompute pipeline and provide validation scripts? I'll handle invoice adjustments and customer notices.
Sam G: I’ll take the recompute. Plan is: replay raw events, run the v2 tokenizer (same as production), run reconciliation, and produce an adjustments file. Draft snippet below.
Rory L: Found root cause: the metering consumer committed offsets prematurely when a deserialization error happened; as a result ~3.9k events were never processed. Filed ENG-SRE-4899 to add durable commit and add dead-lettering for bad events.
eng-sre-bot: ENG-SRE-4899 created. ETA: Fri EOD. Added alert: consumer error rate >0.5% and unprocessed-event backlog >2k.
billing-bot: Scan complete: 9 invoices with deltas >$200, 2 invoices >$4k. Internal sheet: https://redwood.example/sheets/billing_recompute_1791124601 (internal).
Sam G: Initial recompute runbook (to refine):
```
1) Pull raw metering events: metering-store query --from 2026-02-19 --to 2026-02-24 --format=ndjson
2) Run tools/token_recompute.py --mode=v2 --input=events.ndjson --output=recompute.csv
3) Generate reconciliation: tools/reconcile.py recompute.csv original_ledger.csv --out=diff.csv
4) Produce adjustments: tools/prepare_adjustments.py diff.csv --policy=finance-approved --dry-run
5) Submit to billing-api /v1/adjustments --dry-run true; review results
6) Sample 15 customers across small/med/large for manual verification
```
I'll add checksums and a signed manifest for the run so we can audit the change.
Mira K: For invoice edits: we should cap automatic credits to $2k/customer; anything above requires manual exec + legal sign-off. Priya, ok?
Priya (Legal): Agree to cap. For credits >$2k we need a written justification and a standard credit agreement template. We can turn reviews around in ~48 hours once Mira files the packet.
Alex P: Let's set safety thresholds: do not apply if (a) total negative delta >1.5% company MRR, (b) a single customer delta >8% of their monthly tokens, or (c) discrepancy affects >15% of invoices in a billing batch. Any of these triggers a pause and exec review.
Sam G: Will add those thresholds into the runbook and implement a gated apply flow: dry-run -> QA sample -> approval -> apply. Also adding a rollback plan that records pre-adjustment snapshots and can reapply reverse adjustments.
Rory L: I'll add a weekly metering health check job that publishes to the console and fires a page if backfill failure rate > 0.1% for 24h. Also will set up a small perf test to simulate consumer errors.
eng-sre-bot: Dashboard added: "Metering: consumer durable-commit". Weekly alert scheduled.
Mira K: Timeline proposal: Sam posts full runbook Tue EOD, infra fixes by Thu, staging dry-run Fri, customer adjustments next Wed. Any conflicts?
Alex P: That works. Add a Friday status sync until closure. I'll own customer comms and the final sign-off after Mira's QA.
Sam G: I'll include a verification checklist and the exact git sha for tools/token_recompute.py. Also include a script to compute per-customer token delta percentage.
Mira K: I'll prepare the adjustments spreadsheet and tag impacted account managers. Will include suggested PR language for customer emails.
Priya (Legal): If any enterprise customer requests a formal letter, send to legal@redwood.example and we'll provide the signed template.
billing-bot: Scheduling follow-up: reminder in 6 days for owners' updates.
Alex P: Thanks all. Please update the postmortem with ticket links (ENG-SRE-4899, FIN-2712) and owner ETAs. We'll reconvene Friday.
